utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D465 is not admitted into evidence. It is marked, not admitted. Then I'd like to now read the reasons for a decision admitting ten documents from the bar table. The Chamber will now provide reasons for its decision to admit documents now numbered D1120 to D1129 under seal, referenced at pages 20.096 and 20.097 of the trial transcript. These reasons were requested by the Prosecution in an informal communication sent to the Chamber on the 8th of June, 2012. The ten documents are excerpts of larger reports and were tendered as part of the Stanisic Defence bar table motion of the 17th of February, 2012. The Prosecution responded to the motion on the 23rd of March. The Simatovic Defence did not make any submissions in respect of the motion. The documents concern actions taken by various agencies against Serbian and Croatian extremism during the years 1990 to 1995. Each document was identified by the Stanisic Defence as illustrating both positive and negative conclusions supporting their case, thus being relevant. The Prosecution objected to the admission of these documents, stating that the documents lack context because they are excerpts of larger documents and, as a result, their probative value, and I quote: "Is diminished to the point where the materials cannot be reasonably relied upon for the reasons put forth or to exclude the involvement of the Serbian DB in additional activities, as alleged in the Third Amended Indictment." In particular, the Prosecution objected to the admission of the excerpts to draw a negative inference, contending that such inferences cannot be reasonably drawn or relied upon in the absence of the full report. The relevant law for admitting documents from the bar table is Rule 89 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence which provides, in part, that a chamber may admit any relevant evidence which it deems to have probative value; and may exclude evidence if its probative value is substantially outweighed by the need to ensure a fair trial. Further, the Chamber also requires that the tendering party must be able to demonstrate, with clarity and specificity, where and how each document fits into its case. That a document is an excerpt of a larger document is not a reason in itself to bar its admission into evidence. The Trial Chamber found that these documents were sufficiently probative to be admitted from the bar table and that, for each document, the Stanisic Defence had adequately identified with sufficient clarity and specificity its contents, why in its view it is relevant, and to which aspect of its case it relates to. However, the Chamber considered that all parties should have access to the larger documents so as to enable them to contextualise any tendered portions, especially where a negative inference is sought. In this respect, during last week's housekeeping session at pages 20.062 and 20.063 of the trial transcript, it was confirmed by both the Stanisic Defence and the Prosecution that the latter had access to the entire reports from which these documents were excerpted. The Chamber deemed that these documents met the standard for admission set out in Rule 89 of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence and therefore admitted them into evidence from the bar table; however, the Chamber does note that, although these documents meet the standard for admission, it may be especially problematic to rely upon a relatively small portion of a document to show that something did not occur because the document makes no reference to it. And this concludes the Chamber's reason. There is another decision which I will deliver, although the disposition of that decision, I think, has been already communicated with the parties in the Status Conference on Thursday, the 7th of June. It is the decision on the Prosecution motion to admit rebuttal expert testimony and expert report filed on the 8th of May, 2012. In this motion, the Prosecution seeks to call as rebuttal evidence proposed expert witnesses Berger and Meuwly from the Netherlands Forensic Institute and to tender their expert report and CVs. In doing so, the Prosecution seeks to rebut Stanisic Defence expert Brown's evidence. Browne testified as an expert witness in relation to the Mladic notebooks. The Chamber has admitted Book 16 of the Mladic notebook in its entirety as D767. Book 16 was tendered by the Stanisic Defence during Witness Browne's testimony. In his report, Browne emphasise the damage to Book 16. I refer to paragraphs 54 through 59 and Section 5 of his report. In addition, the Chamber has admitted various excerpts from the notebooks as Prosecution exhibits. Browne's report challenges the reliability of these notebooks. The Prosecution contends that Browne's credibility and the weight to be attached to his report are significant issues arising from the Defence case which it could not have anticipated. Neither the Stanisic, nor the Simatovic Defence, responded to this request. The Appeals Chamber has held that rebuttal evidence must be highly probative and must relate to a significant issue arising directly out of evidence -- Defence evidence which could not have been reasonably anticipated. This can be found in the Naletilic and Martinovic Judgement of the 3rd of May, 2006, paragraph 258. The Chamber considers the following relevant factors. First, the Chamber understands that the Prosecution seeks to challenge Browne's methodology and conclusions rather than his factual observations regarding the notebooks. In this respect, the Chamber notes that expert witnesses Berger and Meuwly were asked to review Browne's report based on the information contained in the report itself and without reviewing the original notebooks. Second, Browne was cross-examined at length about his methodology and conclusions. The Prosecution had ample opportunity to prepare for and challenge Brown's evidence during the Defence case in court and made use thereof. In addition, the parties will have further opportunity to make submissions regarding the weight to be attached to this evidence in their final briefs, and/or closing arguments. For these reason, the Chamber considers that the issue of Browne's methodology has been explored in depth and was dealt with comprehensively during the Defence case. The assistance to be expected from the testimony of two additional expert witnesses or an additional expert report regarding Browne's methodology and conclusions is not such as to warrants the proffered rebuttal evidence. Under these circumstances, the request does not meet the standard for rebuttal. Consequently, the Chamber denies the Prosecution's request for leave to present the aforementioned rebuttal evidence. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. I move on to the next item on my agenda. And I would like to invite the Prosecution to specify which of Exhibits P3146 up to and including 3156 need to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that is part of the documentation we received pursuant to our request from the state. And if Mr. Farr wishes to see that, this is part of a large number of documents which we received regarding the intercepted conversations by the Republic of Serbia of Daniel Snedden, and then we received those documents pursuant to our Request for Assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, we generally do request the opportunity to briefly look at the correspondence. If we could have that opportunity, we could revert to the Chamber very shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we move to the last one, which is now D1291. There, we were waiting for a translation. Mr. Bakrac, any translation uploaded?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I understood you correctly, D1291?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. A report on the results of the application of a measure with subject "Farisej" signed by the witness, which was, until five minutes ago, known under the number D902?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If I may clarify, this is 2D. It's 65 ter 2D00459.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is any translation uploaded, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is. Then D1291 is admitted into evidence. We will take a short break. After the break, Mr. Farr, we expect further information about whether those ten documents would need to be under seal. During the break, the Chamber will look in more detail at D868 to see whether it was already admitted or not yet admitted on the basis of a written bar table motion. And the Prosecution has an opportunity to inspect any correspondence related to D1290, known until recently under the number D901. The Chamber, however, before taking a break, would like to know whether the parties would want to raise any further matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have three corrected translations that were resulted either from a Chamber inquiry or from a query both of the parties. We have uploaded revised translations. Those relate to P974, P2401, and P2546.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No other matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Apologies, one more. P3169 as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that makes four documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And one more as well, Your Honour. P3123.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm now at five, Mr. Farr. In football stadiums, people are always crying for ten. I'll not do that. So it stays at five, the score.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: It will stay there for now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, Madam Registrar, perhaps during the break you could verify whether the corrected translations are in your possession. Any other matters to be raised by the Stanisic Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any other matter to be raised by the Simatovic Defence? Any other matter that I referred to earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will take a break. I'm looking at you, Mr. Farr. How much time would you need for the whether or not under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have actually gotten a note. I can answer that right now or immediately after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whatever is done now is already completed. What we would need, Mr. Farr, is information about P3146 up to and including 3156. So that is for 11 documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, five of those documents should be under seal. They are P3147, P3148, P3152, P3155, and P3156.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All the others are public documents. Madam Registrar, would you please take care that 3147, 3148, 3152, 3155 and 3156 are kept under seal. You don't need further time for that. Mr. -- how much time -- do you have the information the Prosecution would like to have a look at in relation to the monitoring of phone calls from Daniel Snedden? Do you have that information readily available so that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm looking at it right now, the list of 111 documents that we received. My colleague and I are looking at it and we're trying to identify these two, the two that are in question, and we'll try to let Mr. Farr know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would 15 minute do to look at it and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Registrar, were you already able to verify whether the new, the corrected translations for P974 and the other four numbers mentioned by Mr. Farr are received and uploaded?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I would just need some reference to numbers under which they are uploaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I suggest that Mr. Farr gives that to you during the break. And that we would resume at 4.25, and then it will only be a matter of minutes to conclude this housekeeping session. We take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A few issues left. D868, which is marked for identification. What is the -- Madam Registrar, could you tell us what the -- what the doc ID -- what the 65 ter number is.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] 65 ter number is 1D2002, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. In the second decision on the bar table motion filed by the Stanisic Defence on the 17th of February, in paragraph 17, under 1, I read it is admitted into evidence the documents bearing, and then among those numbers, 1D02002. Therefore, Madam Registrar, could it be that those dispositions have not yet been fully -- been included in e-court; or is it that -- is a number known already for this document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It was mentioned only verbal. It has existed D number MFI'd and it's been updated in e-court now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that it is now known in e-court still as D868.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that now new number had be to assigned to it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And it's indicated in the Registry's memo that the number was already preassigned so that it didn't receive a new number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Therefore, there's no need -- there was no need to make further submissions on D868 because it was admitted already in evidence. Then, next one, D666, video. Has it been -- Madam Registrar, were you informed by the Prosecution about the exhibit number and have you been able to verify whether it is uploaded into e-court, at least the transcript both in B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, numbers that the Prosecution indicated in previous session have been released now, so I was able to locate it and I was provided during the break with the video of the full document D666.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So nothing opposes admission anymore. D666 is admitted into evidence. The last one, was the Prosecution in a position to verify over the break the information on the origin of D1290, earlier known as D901.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: We were, Your Honour, and we withdraw our objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1290 is admitted into evidence. If I'm not mistaken, there's nothing left at this moment. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour. Your Honour, yes, my mistake, so I kindly ask that we make this correction. D506 was admitted last week and was uploaded as 2D910.1. So could it please be replaced by 2D901.2. Sorry, 910.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please refresh my recollection. D560 is what and what was the reason for it to be replaced?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, D572 was supposed to be taken out of the table - that is that table with Witness Lucic - so was D572; that was supposed to be moved out. That was done. And 2D910.2 is this new version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm a bit lost perhaps. You said the following, Mr. Bakrac: D506 was admitted last week and was uploaded as 2D910.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Your Honour, perhaps it's my mistake. I wasn't following. D560 is the actual number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that's what I read out but possibly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's at least what I heard. Because I then said D560 is what, and what was the reason for it to be replaced? And then you continued but with the reference to D572. Is that one of the documents to be removed from the table which is D560 and that once it was removed from D572 --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, Your Honour. Once that is removed, without that document, is 2D910.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now I see that I earlier made a mistake again. Where I said one of the documents to be removed from the table which is D560, and once D572 was removed, D560 was ready to be admitted, if I understand you well. And then D560 now has received a different document ID which is now 2D910.2, and that is the version without D572. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you received the new version of D560.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, it's available in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it may replace the previous document which was 2D910.1, so the .2 version replaces it, and I think then there's nothing which would further oppose admission. D560 is admitted into evidence. Any need to have it under seal, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I do apologise. Just a second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that it doesn't really have to be under seal. It's a list of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, if at least, even on a list it can be -- it can -- may be a need, but if you say so then it's your exhibit. And, therefore, it is a public document, D560. Having dealt with everything, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, there's one more thing, Your Honour. It's concerning a document which is attached to D431. At the moment 1D3565 is attached and, in fact, that should be replaced by 1D3565.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you refresh my memory what D431 is and what caused the change?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I might have to ask. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Harbour, you're taking over the responsibilities of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes, if I can assist, Your Honour. D431 is an Official Note, and it was originally tendered as a copy, a photocopy of a note retrieved from a published book. And subsequently the Stanisic Defence obtained the original version of that note which they uploaded, but currently that original version has not yet been attached to the exhibit in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it not to be attached but to replace the uploaded version.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has no effect on the translation. It is literally the same which one would expect.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I have not verified that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, if you replaces the original by another one at least there is a need to briefly verify whether the text is the same, because, otherwise, the translation would have --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think we have verified, but I can check that and let Your Honours know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the assumption that it has been verified and both parties could have a look at it. We already allow the replacement of the present version of D431, which is 1D3565, by the new version, which is 1D3565.1. Any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just need to add one document to the list of the five documents for which we have revised translations available. The sixth document is P676.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, we have now six -- we will not go to ten, Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I think it's six.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's really six. It remains at six, the score. Madam Registrar, were you able to verify whether you have received translations for a the six documents referred to by Mr. Farr?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have received translations for all six documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you may replace the present translation and attach the new translations to the exhibits. Any other matter? It's -- it's -- it sounds like a conspiracy. From every corner, someone is on his feet and ... Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the last matter that I will bring to your attention. During Witness Osman Selak's testimony, the Defence tendered a number of underlying documents and they were tendered provisionally under seal out of an abundance of caution and I have subsequently verified that all of them can be public exhibits. So if Your Honour would like, I can read out the exhibit numbers -- or the exhibit ranges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. How long is the list?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: In terms of ranges, three ranges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. If you then please read it slowly so that our transcriber and our interpreters are able to follow you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: D701. That's the first range. It's just one document. The second range is D703 up to and including D729. And the final range is D731 up to and including D740.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. They were confidential at the request of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: At the request of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of the Chamber. That's -- and we asked you to verify whether there was any reason to ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: The Chamber indicated at the time that they should be verified, did not state who should, but since they were Prosecution documents - received from the Prosecution, I should say, not tendered by the Prosecution - I verified them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, under those circumstances, the under-seal status of D701; D703 up to and including D729; and D731 up to and including D740, is changed in public. Madam Registrar, you are hereby invited to make those changes in e-court. I hardly dare to ask whether there's any other matter? No. Apparently there is not. We have not yet scheduled our next hearing. Therefore, we adjourn sine die.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.47 p.m.,
